correctness.rationale: For arbitrary arrays A,B the random permutation linear statistics X_A=sum_i a_(i,Pi(i)) satisfy Cov(X_A,X_B)=(n-1)^-1 sum_ij a^circle_ij b^circle_ij by direct same-index/different-index sampling and double centering. Take A=(i-j)^2 and B=|i-j|, use row/column sums and cubic distance sums to obtain Cov(F,D)=n(n+1)(n^2+1)/30; analogous centered-square calculation gives Var(F)=(n+1)(2n^2+7)/45 and Var(D)=n^2(n-1)(n+1)^2/36. Applying the affine transformation R=1-6D/[n(n^2-1)] yields exact covariance/correlation and the nonzero limit. Independently enumerated EVERY n! permutation for n=2..7 and recomputed exact mixed moments with fractions. This bounded enumeration does not prove all n, which follows from the centering identity and polynomial sums.

value.rationale: Footrule and rho are two canonical rank-disagreement summaries with no ties; the exact finite-sample null correlation quantifies how much duplicate information they encode, and its strong asymptotic anticorrelation persists rather than vanishing. The natural all-n mixed invariant is independently useful as a null calibration benchmark, even though double-centering is the standard proof method.

final_claim: For uniform permutations n>=2, standard L1 Spearman footrule F, squared displacement D, and no-ties Spearman rho R=1-6D/[n(n^2-1)], Cov(F,D)=n(n+1)(n^2+1)/30; Corr(F,R)=-3(n^2+1)/sqrt(5(n-1)(n+1)(2n^2+7)), limiting -3/sqrt(10).
limitations: Only uniform complete rankings without ties and unweighted L1 footrule, ordinary squared displacement/rho.
No claim for partial rankings, tied ranks or nonuniform permutation alternatives.
